subject: Intermittent chunked-transfer/timeouts during NovaFlow POC — exec sync requested
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@novaflow.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: tom.rios@novaflow.com, sre@novaflow.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 08:12:03 -0700
Subject: Demo: streaming stops after ~12s, client sees timeouts

Hey Olga —

Quick note from this morning's product demo / POC session (10:00 PT): we saw repeated interruptions when using your streaming endpoint. Symptoms: tokens stream for ~10–18s, then the client receives a 504 or the WS just shows no more chunks and the UI spinner stays on. When it fails we also see a spike in client-side error counts (connection resets) and the demo app had to fall back to non-streaming polling.

Attached is the lightweight trace we grabbed (novaflow_sinatra_trace.log) and a screenshot from our SRE dashboard (sre_latency_graph.png) — you can see the moment the token stream stops coincides with a latency spike. This is blocking our ability to demonstrate the realtime features today; our product team is escalating. Can your engineering team triage ASAP?

What we tried on our side:
- Switched from WS streaming to chunked SSE — same behavior after ~15s
- Lowered concurrency from 8 -> 2 threads per client — reduced frequency but still reproducible

Happy to hop on a call. We need a short-term workaround (e.g., explicit retry/heartbeat guidance) and an ETA on a fix.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Integrations, NovaFlow
alyssa@novaflow.com

Hi Alyssa —

Thank you for the quick heads-up and the logs/screenshots. I'm very sorry this impacted the demo. We've pulled Rishi and Karthik in to triage; I'm escalating to our on-call engineering lead as well.

Immediate plan:
- Rishi will correlate your trace with our front-door logs and the model backend traces.
- If we can reproduce quickly we'll push a short-lived mitigation (lower max-concurrency for your tenant + extend keepalive/heartbeat) to keep your demo working.
- We'll propose an MA (mutual action) that includes a workaround + permanent fix timeline; draft attached (ma_action_plan_v1.pdf).

Can you confirm: which model variant were you using for the demo, and did you pin any routing policy? That helps us narrow the kernel selection path. Also please share the SDK version and whether the client was using WebSocket or SSE for the failing runs (you noted both tried).

I'll set a 30-minute sync at 16:00 PT to walk through findings unless you need something sooner.

—Olga

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:30:17 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo: streaming stops after ~12s, client sees timeouts

Olga / team —

I pulled the attached trace and our front-door logs for the same window. Key observations:
- We see a tail-latency spike on the inference path starting ~2026-09-29T15:08:42Z coincident with multiple upstream 502/504 from the proxy layer.
- The client-side traces in novaflow_sinatra_trace.log show the streaming TCP connection stays open but token frames stop being emitted from the runtime; no explicit process crash.
- Proxy logs indicate an increased number of concurrent keepalive timeouts and a backlog of epoll events on the node serving the tenant (upstream 10.1.2.45:443).

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: a regression in our batching scheduler + proxy backpressure under high per-tenant concurrency. The runtime's continuous-batching path appears to hit a shim where the kernel-level socket pool starves the worker thread that flushes chunked frames.

Short-term mitigations I recommend (can be pushed within 2 hours):
1) Lower per-tenant concurrency cap from 32 -> 8 for NovaFlow (config push). This reduces burst contention on the batcher.
2) Increase HTTP keepalive + WS heartbeat to 60s to prevent premature proxy teardown.
3) Enable an aggressive KV-prefix cache for their traffic profile to reduce model compute for repeated prefixes (runtime flag).

Longer-term: patch the scheduler to avoid long-lived epoll backlogs when many sockets become idle but registered (I have a draft patch — commit 3f2a9d1 that I can submit for review).

Attaching the matching logs (novaflow_sinatra_trace.log) and a zoomed latency graph (sre_latency_graph.png). I'll start the config change on a canary node and report back.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Team / execs (looping Jon and product leadership via separate thread) —

Summary: NovaFlow (strategic POC / high-value account) experienced reproducible streaming interruptions during their product demo this morning. The interruption pattern points to chunked-transfer stalls where the socket stays open but token emission stops; we observed correlated proxy 504s and elevated error rates. Customer-facing impact: demo failure and product team escalation (Alyssa).

Customer asks:
- Fast mitigation to allow demo to complete and avoid canceling their evaluation
- Root-cause timeline and ETA for rollback/permanent fix
- Consideration for a goodwill credit or extended trial window if we cannot fully mitigate in <48 hours

Immediate asks for leadership:
- Approval to offer a one-month credit if the customer requests (we've used precedent for POC-impacting infra incidents).
- Priority review for Rishi's scheduler patch; if acceptable, expedite CI/merge + canary deploy.

Rishi has a concrete mitigation path and has started a canary config change. Karthik, please own customer comms on the pricing/credit ask. Olga, keep Alyssa updated and run the 16:00 PT sync.

I'll draft a short exec note after the 16:00 sync to share with Sales/CS leads.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Reliability & Sales Engineering

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Demo: streaming stops after ~12s, client sees timeouts — action items and 17:00 PT call

Alyssa / team —

Thanks again for the trace and patience. Quick update and actions:

What we did (15:30–16:10 PT):
- Applied per-tenant concurrency cap to NovaFlow (32 -> 8) on canary nodes; observation window showed the token stream stayed stable for 20+ minutes on canary.
- Increased keepalive/heartbeat intervals in the proxy for the tenant to 60s.
- Enabled runtime aggressive KV-prefix cache flag for their traffic pattern.

Open items:
- Rishi will push the scheduler patch to CI for review (in progress).
- Karthik will draft the credit offer and coordinate with Sales Ops (internal).
- Marissa will prepare the exec blurb and approve the credit threshold.

Please join the 17:00 PT quick sync (link: https://meet.redwood.com/olga/novaflow-esc-20260929). Goal: short postmortem, confirm canary stability, and agree on customer comms.

If the canary holds we'll roll to their production tenancy tonight under a blue/green window. Apologies again for the disruption — we'll confirm next steps during the call.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
